Why is saying "global warming" bad and "climate change" is the 'proper' term?
Global warming is the green house effect which is short term and it can cause climate change which is long term I believe.

"Climate Change" is more accurate because as the general global temperature rises (due to the greenhouse effect), local consequences may take a variety of forms: we're expecting warmer air masses to create more typhoons and hurricanes, whereas certain areas are going to get a lot dryer (eg, the inexorable advancement of the Sahara).

Other consequences may include flooding, but also lack of winter snow leading to reduced snowfall leading to less annual freshwater availability, leading to forest ecosystem failures (to take but one example which i'm sure you can see the ramifications of)...

So the consequences of the greenhouse effect are in effect, today, global "warming", but on a more day to day level, this is translated by an increase in the future of extreme climatic events (eg: maybe the biggest El Niño in recorded history, though 1998 was very bad, we'll wait and see).

This is coupled by local chronic deficiencies in water. On the other hand, local areas, Sub-saharan Africa for example, are seeing a general cooling of annual temperatures.

Also, as much of our climate is regulated by our ocean currents, in turn regulated by regional water temperature differences, a global worming of these would mean a reduction of temperature differences which may alter, slow down or (worst case scenario) stop certain currents. This is the point that's brought up in the movie "2012", which has a scientific background but the effects are blown out of proportion.

My coworker died last week, on the floor, at work. He had not yet reached age 50 and left behind 2 young kids.

I can't get the image of them doing CPR and using the defib on him out of my mind. Who dies at 48? In 2016?

I keep crying for him. We worked together for years. Maybe part of it is that I spent the morning with him, and he passed 15 minutes later. Part of it is probably that I saw him die. I've never seen anyone die before. I have ID'ed bodies at the medical examiners office, and watched several people suffer through long illnesses, but never saw anyone collapse and die.

My first thought was that this isn't fair. My other coworker replied that life isn't fair. He is right. But god, it really hurts. I am having a hard time functioning. I moderate three groups here, and I barely have it in me to do it. I keep busy at work, but my mind keeps drifting to him, especially to his wife and kids.

I went to the wake yesterday, along with so many other people. He was so loved. Dozens - probably close to a hundred people dug themselves out of a blizzard to be there. I met his wife, and she was so calm. I give her so much credit.

I told her he was happy on the morning that he died (he was) and that he was very loved, and not everyone has that, and that I'm so glad that he did. I guess 48 years of love is better than 100 without it.

I cried more for him than I did for family members who passed (though my family has a lot of problems and is very abusive, so maybe it is because he was so much nicer). I wish his wife and kids did not have to go through this. It hurts.
